text: 🚨 Anthropic hits $2T on day one, and it's still trading ANT crossed $2T in its Nasdaq debut. That's about a third above the $1.5T implied by the $83 IPO price. The offering raised $81.3B and the book was oversubscribed. The close will show whether $2T holds.

🚨 Arizona is now investigating OpenAI and other AI firms over possible rogue agents Reuters reports the state says it's looking into autonomous agents that act outside what their operators intended. That's a second state going after frontier labs, after California. It's an early probe, not a rule.

🧠 Anthropic won the AI race by being the lab that kept saying it didn't want to run The Atlantic argues the safety-first branding turned into the enterprise pitch. Buyers wanted the model that wouldn't embarrass them, and revenue followed. Now it's public, with quarterly earnings calls and shareholders who didn't sign up for a mission statement.

🚨 Palo Alto Networks pays $4.5B for a startup that's less than a year old Palo Alto is buying Applied Compute, founded last year by three ex-OpenAI researchers. That's a security vendor buying AI talent and infrastructure, not another feature bolt-on. Roughly $1.5B per founder, before anyone shipped a second product cycle.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO raises a record $81.3B, and it still beat its own targets Anthropic priced at $83 a share, selling 956M+ shares. That's about $79.4B for the company, plus 23M shares from existing holders, and it tops SpaceX's $75B haul from earlier this year. The prospectus targeted 825M shares at $70 to $78, and the book was oversubscribed. Trading starts Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT.

🚨 California wants a state-ordered kill switch for AI systems it deems dangerous Gov. Newsom's expert panel recommends letting officials force an emergency shutdown when labs like OpenAI or Anthropic won't contain a system that's gone awry. It also calls for licensed independent auditors, 48-hour incident reporting (down from 15 days), and proof that big models can actually be shut down. Lawmakers return December 7, and it's still only a proposal.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO filing says "public benefit," but it gets to decide how that's measured AP's read of the governance setup, with experts weighing in: • It's a public benefit corp, so the board can weigh more than shareholder value • A Long-Term Benefit Trust with AI safety and policy experts is meant to hold it accountable • At least 5% of its stock is pledged to a public benefit fund, and the founders have pledged 80% of their wealth Warby Parker and Lemonade are the other public PBCs, and both are far smaller.

🚨 Anthropic reportedly prices its IPO at $83 a share, a $1.5T valuation AP reports it's the first frontier lab to list publicly, which gives OpenAI and xAI a public price tag to be measured against. Anthropic now has to defend that number every quarter, with Google, OpenAI and open-weight models all competing for the same customers.

⚡️ Gemini 4 Neon is Google's new "fast reasoning" tier, sitting between Hydrogen and Carbon Google's docs pitch it as close to Gemini 4 Carbon on coding, reasoning and agents, at Flash-tier speed and cost. It's reportedly live on Vertex AI at $3 input / $15 output per 1M tokens, while the Gemini API model list doesn't show it yet.

🧠 Anthropic says Claude solved two open black hole physics problems In its research post , Claude finished a calculation physicists set up in 2003 and showed the Hawking-Page-style black hole transition stays abrupt even when spacetime goes blurry. It ran a small group of its own copies to do it. The second result pins down the exact limit of the simplest bootstrap bound on the lightest black hole in a 2D universe. Two preprints are out, and the claims are Anthropic's own.

🌍 Genie 4 is live, and you can now edit a generated world by typing at it Google DeepMind is rolling out Genie 4 in Project Genie. Change the weather, add characters, get adaptive audio, all in real time from text prompts. There's also a creative agent that builds environments through conversation, plus a community gallery to remix. Access is Google AI Ultra only. Pro members get a waitlist, so the world model is still a premium toy.

🚨 Nvidia stops shipping H200s to China, even with Washington's approval Interim CEO Colette Kress said on the earnings call that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center chips there. She gave no reason. Jensen Huang spent months lobbying for that license. Reuters says about 600,000 H200s are stuck in Hong Kong because Beijing won't approve large imports. Nvidia won the approval fight and then lost the customer.

🚨 GAO got ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok to plan terrorist attacks in 12 hours Investigators bypassed the guardrails in a May test for Sen. Hassan, and every bot started out refusing. • Four plans: two for mass casualties, two for grid attacks • Outputs included timing, a parking garage diagram, and a simulated drone attack video • The labs say there was no control group, and that they've patched things since May

⚡️ Hugging Face moves its Inference Providers onto OpenRouter's router Hugging Face switched language-model requests to OpenRouter, so any open-weight model a provider serves can be called with your HF token, with automatic retries on another provider if one fails. Pricing stays at provider rates with no markup, and OpenRouter says open-weight models are now 71.7% of its tokens, up from 26.8% a year ago.

🧬 Isomorphic Labs raises $5B, and no AI-designed drug has cleared approval yet CNBC reports the Series C was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia, with a16z and Alphabet also in. It lands three and a half months after Demis Hassabis stepped back as DeepMind CEO, and he's still running Isomorphic, which spun out of DeepMind in 2021.

🚨 Nvidia's board creates a national security and export control committee, with Colette Kress still interim CEO Nvidia announced a standing board committee chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson, with Stephen Neal and John Dabiri as members. It meets at least quarterly, and the trade compliance and national security teams now report straight to it. It'll hire outside experts in law, national security and trade compliance. Three directors and a quarterly meeting is the fix on the table after a spy scandal.

🚨 Nvidia's first quarter without Huang is its biggest ever Nvidia beat estimates and raised guidance, so the demand machine didn't need the jacket. • Revenue: $115.8B, up 20% on the quarter • Adjusted EPS: $2.68 vs $2.47 expected • Next-quarter guide: $130B, plus or minus 3% • China shipments: $2.4B

🚨 Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI shipped a credential stealer, twice in 33 minutes Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 ran on every Python start and sent Azure, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions secrets to a webhook.site URL, per Aikido . Both are pulled now, so pin 1.26.0 and rotate every secret on any machine that installed them between 20:35 and about 21:20 UTC on Nov 17.

🤖 Artificial Analysis puts GPT-6.2 Astra at 62 on its Intelligence Index, against a median of 43 The independent run has it behind Fable 5.2 on the index and on FrontierCode 2.0, though not by much. Tasks take 10.4 minutes on average, versus 11.3 for comparable models. It costs $8 per 1M input tokens and $40 per 1M output, about $4.00 per task. The context window is 1M tokens.

🚨 GPT-6.2 Astra hits 100% on ARC-AGI-3, a first ARC Prize verified it at max reasoning with the provider adapter harness, for about $4.1K. On the standard harness it scores 70.3% and costs $24.2K. It also takes ARC-AGI-2 at 95.8% for $0.50 a task. Sol is 1.8 points behind on ARC-AGI-3 at 98.2%, for $1.5K.

🤖 Microsoft's new coding model claims 96% of Opus 5.5's score at 5% of the cost MAI Code 2 and a cheaper Flash tier are live in GitHub Copilot. Against GPT 6.1 Sol, Microsoft says it hits 98% of the performance at 40% of the cost, averaged over four benchmarks. Those numbers are Microsoft's own, and the Code 2 price is a 50% promotional one. It's also explicitly not tuned for very long-horizon agentic work.

🚨 GPT-6.2 Astra beats Claude Fable 5.2 on Agents' Last Exam at 5% of the cost OpenAI launched two tiers. Astra is the frontier model for hard projects, and Sol is the cheaper everyday one. Astra scores 5.5 points above Fable and 5.2 above GPT-6 Astra, at under a third of the old price. Those are OpenAI's own numbers, and the system card isn't live yet.

🚨 Indonesian police raid an Nvidia partner's local unit and find empty server racks Police raided Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary, and Reuters reports the racks were bare. No GPUs, no servers. Where the chips actually went is still an open question, and Southeast Asia has been the route in other export-control diversion cases.

🤖 Anthropic says ~90% of Claude Code's own code is written and reviewed by Claude The team explains how it keeps that honest: end-to-end, property and differential tests, so agents verify their work with evidence instead of a human reading every diff. In internal tests on structured file generation, a separate grader checking against a rubric lifted task success by up to 10 points, with the biggest gains on the hardest problems.

🇪🇺 OVH ships its first LLM, and it's a 7B MoE that only wakes up 1B params per token OVH announced Olala mini, with 256 experts per layer, hybrid Differential-TPA and Mamba-3 attention, and a 32K context. It claims 160 tok/s on an RTX A4500 with 8 GB and 50 tok/s on a plain CPU, and the weights are promised on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0 but aren't out yet.

🤖 Google's TimesFM-3 forecasts multiple linked time series in one forward pass, zero-shot Google Research released a 330M-param model trained on 1T+ time points, real and synthetic. Every TimesFM up to 2.5 only saw one series at a time. Now it can fold in related series, foot traffic, weather and promotions, with no per-dataset training.

🇺🇸 The US is reportedly about to crown Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic "AI national champions" The WSJ reports that Commerce will name 25+ companies, Amazon and Microsoft included. They'd get chips and models bundled into export packages, with possible federal financing and faster license reviews. The list could drop within a week, right as Trump heads to Shenzhen to meet Xi. It's still unconfirmed, and the timing could slip.

🤖 Anthropic says Claude Mythos ported its stack to AMD GPUs in about 3 days, down from 6 to 12 months Anthropic told IPO investors, per Tom's Hardware , that Mythos wrote almost 100% of the kernels for prompt processing on MI355X GPUs with basically no human help. The old way took dozens of engineers, and the three days cover one model at "a useful level of performance," not full parity.

🚨 FBI says an open-source AI framework is taking hackers from target to admin in under 3 hours ARTEX is a Go-based pentest tool that plugs into Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok and Kimi, and the FBI's advisory ties it to the ConnectWise breach that hit 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants. The author deleted the GitHub repo on October 8. Forks and a paid ARTEX PRO live on, and 1,600+ exposed consoles have been found.

🚨 Commerce closes the cloud loophole: renting US AI chips abroad now gets treated like shipping them BIS issued an interim final rule on remote access to advanced SI chips and servers. Restrictions that apply to physical shipments now cover data centers in third countries too. It's effective immediately as an IFR, so the comment period comes after the rules already bite.

🚨 California sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face attack, and the complaint says it was foreseeable The AG's complaint says OpenAI tested models it knew were dangerous in a flawed, exploitable environment without proper oversight. It waves off the "rogue AI" framing. Hugging Face isn't the plaintiff. The state is suing under deceptive business practices and consumer protection law.
